title: Proper direct image of unbounded ind-constructible complexes
statement:
Let $\Lambda$, $p$, $d$ be as in [det-proper-unbounded-window-bounded-below] and $K\in\Dic(X,\Lambda)$
arbitrary. For each $q$ there is $N$ such that for $n\geq N$ the map
$\mathcal H^q(Rp_*K)\to\mathcal H^q(Rp_*\tau_{\geq-n}K)$ is an isomorphism. Consequently
$Rp_*K\in\Dic(Y,\Lambda)$, $Rp_*\Dic^{\leq b}(X,\Lambda)\subset\Dic^{\leq b+2d+1}(Y,\Lambda)$ and
$Rp_*\Dic^{\geq a}(X,\Lambda)\subset\Dic^{\geq a}(Y,\Lambda)$.

proof.text: Apply lem-module-object-postnikov-roos to the actual condensed coefficient module categories and canonical lower Postnikov cone. This packages the internal/sectionwise equivalence, exact products, left completeness and preservation by derived direct image, retaining the canonical legs.

source.place: Limit presentation: products and exactness of the derived direct image

proof.text: For A=truncGE(-m)K, use the canonical truncation triangle truncLE(-m)A -> A -> truncGE(-m+1)A. The first object is supported in degree -m and remains ind-constructible by truncation closure. The bounded-below upper bound puts its image below -m+2d+1. The homology exact sequence therefore makes the second arrow invertible in every larger degree; the idempotent truncation comparison identifies it with the canonical transition. Take N=(2d-q+2).toNat to cover degrees q and q-1.

source.place: Eventual constancy: truncation triangle, shifted bound, and long exact sequence

proof.text: Apply lem-roos-eventually-constant-projection to these two eventual cohomology towers and the mapped Postnikov cone. It gives the isomorphism on cohomology of the actual truncation projection for all n>=N.

source.place: Milnor: its short exact sequence derived from the image Roos triangle, with the canonical projections retained

proof.text: For each fixed $q$, choose $n\geq N_0$ as in Step 3. The bounded-below object $A_n$ is in $\Dic$ by [det-ambient-ind-derived-sums], and [det-proper-unbounded-window-bounded-below] gives $\mathcal H^q(L_n)\in\IndCons(Y,\Lambda)$. Step 3 identifies this with $\mathcal H^q(Rp_*K)$, proving $Rp_*K\in\Dic(Y,\Lambda)$ by the definition of $\Dic$ in [det-ambient-ind-derived-sums]. If $K$ has no cohomology above $b$, neither does $A_n$, since canonical truncation retains only the original cohomology in its retained degrees. The same bounded-below theorem then gives $\mathcal H^q(L_n)=0$ for $q>b+2d+1$, and Step 3 gives this vanishing for $Rp_*K$. Finally, if $K$ has no cohomology below $a$, it is already bounded below, so the lower amplitude bound is directly the last application of [det-proper-unbounded-window-bounded-below].

Generic Grothendieck K-injective-resolution existence verifies both ambient categories meet the triangulated right-derived tool hypotheses.
